nodes.label: Domain-Driven Design Patterns
nodes.rationale: DDD aligns software design with business reality so the code structure mirrors how the business thinks and operates.

nodes.label: Bounded Contexts
nodes.rationale: The same real-world concept means different things per context - Customer is leads and revenue in Sales, tickets and SLAs in Support, invoices and credit limit in Billing - so each context owns its data and logic with no shared database, and may pick its own stack and deployment strategy. Heuristic: if two concepts change for different reasons they belong in different contexts.

nodes.label: Context Mapping Patterns
nodes.rationale: Seven named inter-context relationships (Shared Kernel, Customer-Supplier, Conformist, Anti-Corruption Layer, Open Host Service, Published Language, Separate Ways), each selected by team relationship rather than technology - Conformist when upstream has no incentive to accommodate you, Separate Ways when integration costs more than it returns.

nodes.label: Anti-Corruption Layer
nodes.rationale: Isolates a clean domain model from a legacy or external model by translating between them, so when the external system changes only the ACL needs updating.

nodes.label: Entities
nodes.rationale: Defined by identity that persists across state changes, not by attributes: two customers with the same name are different customers if their IDs differ.

nodes.label: Value Objects
nodes.rationale: Immutable and identity-free - equality is over all attributes, so two Money objects with the same amount and currency are interchangeable. Preferred over primitives because an email is not just a string.

nodes.label: Aggregates and Aggregate Roots
nodes.rationale: Exactly one root per aggregate is the only externally referenceable entity, so all changes route through it and invariants hold. Transactions must not span aggregates and other aggregates are referenced by ID; large aggregates cause contention, so needing a cross-aggregate transaction is a signal the boundaries are wrong.

nodes.label: Domain Events
nodes.rationale: Past-tense facts named EntityPastTenseVerb, carrying event ID, timestamp, aggregate ID and payload-at-the-time. They are the primary integration mechanism between bounded contexts, which is what makes publishers independent of subscribers.

nodes.label: Repository Pattern
nodes.rationale: One repository per aggregate root, interface in the domain layer and implementation in infrastructure, returning fully constituted aggregates. Complex query logic belongs in separate read models rather than in repositories.

nodes.label: Event Storming
nodes.rationale: A seven-step colour-coded workshop (events, commands, actors, aggregates, context boundaries, policies) that surfaces natural bounded-context boundaries, integration points, and complexity hot spots from the domain experts rather than from the code.
